The stub is the #else of HAVE_LINUX_RTNETLINK_H; this build defines it (obj/include/config.h:197) and compiles poll_netlink (rtnetlink socket for address/link/route changes) instead.

learn.microsoft.com search finds no page for it and dlls/apphelp/tests tests only ApphelpCheckShellObject. It returns TRUE (no compatibility entry blocks the package), which is what a machine with an empty compatibility database answers; the meaning of the first argument (ptr) and any other result are unknown. FIXME kept: not a complete implementation.
Same as ApphelpCheckInstallShieldPackage: no Microsoft page (docs search: 0 hits), no Wine test; TRUE = nothing blocks the package; the ptr argument's contract is unknown.

No Microsoft page (docs search: 0 hits) and no Wine test. Wine's own readers fix only the key layout: win32u/sysparams.c:5561 and kernelbase/process.c:693 read HKCU then HKLM Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\AppCompatFlags\Layers, value name = the program's full path, REG_SZ, space-separated layer names. The meaning of its flags, the add/remove-one-layer semantics and the error codes are in no allowed source.

No Microsoft page (docs search: 0 hits), no Wine test; the Layers key layout is known from win32u/sysparams.c:5561 but what the call writes when layers is empty, and its errors, are not. Writing the key by guesswork would change what Wine's own readers apply to a program.
No Microsoft page (docs search: 0 hits), no Wine test; the meaning of flags (which hive is read), the size in/out contract and the error for a too-small buffer are in no allowed source.

Documented (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/devnotes/sdbcreatedatabase: path + PATH_TYPE, returns a PDB or NULL) but a database it creates must be a valid .sdb, and the file format (header, tag stream, tag values) is in no allowed source: the Application Compatibility Database overview defines TAG/TAGID but not the layout. See escalate-7.md.
Documented (devnotes/sdbopendatabase) but returning a handle for a file without checking or decoding it would claim an empty database that may not be; needs the .sdb format. See escalate-7.md.

Documented (devnotes/sdbinitdatabase: HID_* flags, predefined SDB_DATABASE_MAIN_SHIM/MSI/DRIVERS databases) -- its main purpose is to open sysmain.sdb and the other databases, which needs the .sdb reader. See escalate-7.md.
Documented (devnotes/sdbclosedatabase) but there is no PDB to close until SdbOpenDatabase/SdbCreateDatabase return one. Goes with them. See escalate-7.md.

Documented (devnotes/sdbgetfirstchild: returns the first child's TAGID or TAGID_NULL) but a TAGID is a position in the tag stream (overview: 'a pointer to an entry in a particular database'); answering TAGID_NULL for a database that has children would be false. Needs the .sdb format. See escalate-7.md.

Documented (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/devio/installnewdevice) as the Add Hardware wizard: 'the user starts at the detection choice page' / the class selection page, with the reboot status in pReboot. There is no such wizard here; returning TRUE (today) claims a device was installed that was not. See escalate-7.md.

IAppxFactory2, IAppxFactory3 and IAppxFactory4 are documented (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/appxpackaging/nn-appxpackaging-iappxfactory2 ... 4) so a Windows factory answers QueryInterface for them; their IIDs and the vtable order are in no allowed source (Wine's IDL has none; the pages list methods alphabetically). See escalate-7.md.

IAppxPackageWriter is documented (nn-appxpackaging-iappxpackagewriter: AddPayloadFile, Close, ...) but Wine's IDL only forward-declares it: no IID, no vtable order. A writer also needs a block map, [Content_Types].xml and a ZIP writer. See escalate-7.md.

IAppxBlockMapReader (GetFile, GetFiles, GetHashMethod, GetStream), IAppxBlockMapFile/Block and their enumerators are documented but not defined in Wine's IDL: no IIDs, no vtable order. The parser exists (package.c) and would be reused. See escalate-7.md.
Same missing IAppxBlockMapReader definition, plus checking the block map against the package signature (AXBM digest of the AppX SIP, patch 0037). See escalate-7.md.
IAppxBundleFactory2-style newer interfaces: IIDs not in an allowed source (see appx_factory_QueryInterface). See escalate-7.md.
IAppxBundleWriter is documented (nn-appxpackaging-iappxbundlewriter) but only forward-declared in Wine's IDL: no IID, no vtable order. See escalate-7.md.
The package reader's newer interfaces (IAppxPackageReader's siblings, IAppxFilesEnumerator variants): IIDs not in an allowed source. See escalate-7.md.

IAppxPackageReader::GetBlockMap returns an IAppxBlockMapReader, which has no definition in an allowed source (see appx_factory_CreateBlockMapReader). The reader already parses the block map internally. See escalate-7.md.
IAppxBundleReader::GetBlockMap: same missing IAppxBlockMapReader definition. See escalate-7.md.

IAppxManifestReader::GetDeviceCapabilities returns an IAppxManifestDeviceCapabilitiesEnumerator, documented (nn-appxpackaging-iappxmanifestdevicecapabilitiesenumerator) but only forward-declared in Wine's IDL: no IID, no vtable order. The manifest's <DeviceCapability> elements are parsed nowhere yet. See escalate-7.md.
